about.title: La Puente Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a crash is disorienting, and Los Angeles County traffic data won't tell you what to do next. La Puente sees real traffic volume on corridors like Valley Boulevard, Temple Avenue, and Hacienda Boulevard, with reported collisions often clustering on Friday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. When a crash proves fatal, California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. These cases are separate from any criminal proceeding and focus on the financial and emotional toll left behind. We're here to review what happened, explain your options under California's two-year filing deadline, and help you understand whether a claim may be appropriate for your family's circumstances.

whyChoose.title: Why La Puente Families Choose Us

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to spouses, domestic partners, and children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in specific circumstances. We can help clarify where your family stands.

items.title: A Firm Filing Deadline
items.desc: Wrongful death claims generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shortens significantly if a government entity is involved. Reaching out sooner helps preserve your options.

items.title: Recognizing What Can Be Claimed
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance — losses that are easy to overlook while grieving. We can walk through what may apply to your situation.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may be eligible depending on the circumstances. We can review your family's specific situation to clarify who qualifies.

items.question: Is there a deadline for filing after a fatal crash in La Puente?
items.answer: Yes, California generally requires wrongful death claims to be filed within two years of the date of death. If a government entity, such as a public road authority, may be involved, that deadline can be much shorter. It's best to get guidance early so deadlines aren't missed.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim relate to any criminal charges from the crash?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on compensation for the family's losses. It proceeds independently of any criminal case against the at-fault driver. Given that Los Angeles County records collisions on corridors like Amar Road and Temple Avenue each year, families in La Puente sometimes navigate both processes, and we can explain how they interact.

items.question: How do you help my family with a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: We review your case, help you understand your rights under California law, and handle wrongful death matters on contingency — meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.
